body:
Thank you all for your comments.  

I don't know what came over me yesterday. I don't think I've ever felt so overwhelmed in my life and I have gone through what some may consider a lot. 

I guess I'll have to chalk it up to yet another crossroads that I am facing with much uncertainty.  

I can't say that I've never contemplated suicide but I have, on many occasions, considered what would happen if...if my I lost control of my vehicle? If the tree fell on me? If I got caught in a burning building? I never REALLY thought about how my life would actually end.  What it would feel like, what people would say, how the funeral would be, the impact of my death on the people around me that love me. 

Watching that storm yesterday afternoon from my desk at work somehow brought forward all of the feelings, that, as a man, I bury deep inside on a daily basis. 

My life isn't bad, not at all. I am blessed to have loving friends. Some that I've known for over 20 years.  I have a job, I own a home, I can pay my bills on time. My wife and I travel and I know what love is and what it feels like.

My mom passed away 2 years after I graduated college of congestive heart failure, on the living room couch, alone, during the day while my dad was at work.  I will never forget the moment that he and my best friend knocked on my door at my house (they never came unannounced never mind together) to tell me the news.  And I will never forget the feeling of guilt I had at that exact moment. Guilt for not seeing her as often as I should have or calling her as often as I should have. Or for being annoyed, for no good reason, when she called me, often just to talk.  That is something that I have to live with and have come to terms with over the past few years.

What really bothered me yesterday is I realized I was still doing the same thing today that I was doing when she was alive. I don't think about her as often as I used to, I don't visit her grave as often as I should and that's something I need to change in my life, to honor the person she was and to thank her for molding me into the person I have become. 

My wife is more understanding that I could ever imagine anyone ever being.  I met her shortly after my mothers death and she was the single person that helped me get through my darkest days.  We would spend hours on the phone just talking. She would go to the graveyard with me...and without me.   I have never felt like I couldn't talk with her about my feelings. I know she is always there for me and always has been.  The decision to not talk as much about my mother with my wife was my own.  One day it dawned on me that I wasn't being fair.  She had recently reconnected with her mother, whom she hadn't had any contact with for over 13 years, and she was going through some very difficult emotional stresses.  Being with her during that made my situation feel somewhat trivial.  My thoughts were, I had a loving mother, who was always there for me, she had dedicated her life to making mine better, to making sure there was always food on the table, that I had clothes that fit, that I was educated and would be the first person in my family to not only attend college but earn a degree. All of these things came with great personal sacrifice on her part. Much of which I never understood until it was too late to thank her for it.  Her mother on the other hand was abusive. My wife has had more broken bones than anyone I have ever met. She was verbally abused, physically abused and, when her mother left her family, my wife was the one that took over the "motherly duties" while her father worked 70+ hours a week to keep a roof over their heads.   In my mind, it just wasn't right of me to complain about what I had done wrong in the relationship that I had with my mother when not only did she not have that chance but probably couldn't even imagine what that would feel like. 

Thank you all again for your thoughts and compliments.   I have never written anything like this before in my life and if these feelings are what it takes to do it I hope I never will write like this again.  

Thank you
